checkpoint.contextAtWrite: wugs-s4 fully closed out this session. When its E2E checks failed, verified the actual failure reason (job conclusion 'cancelled', a concurrent E2E run 22 seconds apart on the same branch racing for the deploy-group concurrency slot) before re-running, rather than assuming flake blindly -- confirmed the same documented pattern as wugs-s3's earlier failure. Re-run passed cleanly, operator merged, DoD written and pushed. This is now the third and fourth story (wugs-s3, wugs-s4) this session to hit this same CI concurrency flake -- caused by this session's own volume of rapid pushes to both feature branches and master (state/bookkeeping commits). Not a code defect in any story; a known, already-documented characteristic of this repo's CI concurrency design given this session's unusually high push volume.
checkpoint.resumeInstruction: 1) Start the next story in the corrected sequence: wugs-s8 (branch-setup -> implementation-plan -> subagent-execution -> verify-completion -> branch-complete -> DoD, same full cycle as every prior story this session). Read its story/DoR/test-plan artefacts fresh before writing the implementation plan. 2) Continue watching for cross-story merge conflicts on shared functions in src/web-ui/routes/products.js (_renderGuardrailsSection, _renderOrgGuardrailsSection, handleGetProductGuardrailsView, _resolveAllPendingPrs, _renderPieceContent, _renderPromptBox, _trackPendingPr) -- read each new story's Architecture Constraints/File Map to anticipate this before starting; resolve by hand-merging both sides' intent if it happens. 3) If a PR's E2E checks fail, ALWAYS check the actual job conclusion via `gh api repos/heymishy/skills-repo/actions/runs/<run-id>/jobs` before assuming anything -- 'cancelled' (not 'failure') plus a concurrent run on the same branch/deploy-group within ~30 seconds is the established flake signature in this repo (confirmed 3x this session: wugs-s3, wugs-s7's earlier interim run, wugs-s4); re-run via `gh run rerun <run-id> --repo heymishy/skills-repo --failed` once confirmed. A genuine 'failure' conclusion (not 'cancelled') would need real investigation, not a re-run. 4) Consider slowing down the rate of standalone master pushes (pipeline-state.json/decisions.md bookkeeping commits) if practical, since each one competes for the same deploy-group concurrency slot as PR E2E checks and is the root cause of these repeated flakes this session -- bundling multiple small state updates into fewer master pushes where the workflow allows would reduce this friction, though the existing per-task-completion bookkeeping cadence has been deliberate and is not necessarily worth changing given it's non-blocking (just occasionally requires one re-run). 5) Process patterns proven effective all session, keep using them: full implementer -> spec-compliance -> code-quality -> fix -> re-review cycle for tasks with new logic; lighter single-dispatch-plus-self-verify for pure lock-in tasks. Recompute and explicitly state expected test counts to dispatched agents when a plan's own per-task predictions have drifted due to review-added tests in earlier tasks. 6) For every pipeline-state.json write: fetch origin/master first and compare against HEAD before writing directly -- if no drift, safe to write directly. Baseline test count to expect: 33 pre-existing failures out of 513+ files -- confirm the FAILURE LIST matches the documented baseline (not just the count) before assuming any change is pre-existing.
